capture_completion.process_outcome: Harness continuation cancelled the original process after three complete metric polls. Recovery collected owned Lambda logs and verified all owned resources absent without further executions or metric polls.
capture_completion.captured_source_note: probe_source preserves the executed source. The delivered script subsequently normalizes CloudWatch timestamps to UTC in the poll-completion comparison; raw timestamps and results remain unchanged.
missing_evidence: No positive WebSocket IntegrationError sample: proxy status 503 and missing Lambda alias instead produced ExecutionError.
No WebSocket Lambda raised-exception or failed Management callback cohort.
HTTP unmatched-route 404 cohort has no metric datapoints in three bounded polls; absence is not an inferred zero or a universal nonpublication guarantee.
Both one-way sends and Lambda records occurred in 08:23 UTC, but route one metrics were split between 08:23 and 08:24; exact request-to-minute assignment is not established.

measured_contract_notes: HTTP dimensions observed: ApiId; ApiId,Stage; ApiId,Method,Resource,Stage. WebSocket detailed dimensions observed: ApiId,Route,Stage, not the documentation's Method/Resource combination.
HTTP Count uses Unit None and one sample of value 1 per counted request. HTTP 4xx and 5xx also use Unit None and include zero-valued samples for counted non-error requests.
HTTP DataProcessed uses Bytes. HTTP Latency and IntegrationLatency use Milliseconds. IAM-rejected requests had Count,4xx,5xx,DataProcessed,Latency but no IntegrationLatency datapoints.

Every normal HTTP Lambda response, including proxy 400 and 503, matched len(json.dumps(captured response).encode()) exactly: 198,198,216,217,213,210,214,214,220,219 bytes. These values include the proxy envelope and escaped body, not merely the client-visible body.

[INFERENCE] Raised-exception HTTP DataProcessed 270 exactly matches reconstruction of the standard Lambda errorMessage/errorType/requestId/stackTrace envelope from the captured exception log, handler source and invocation ID. The actual error response envelope was not independently captured.

IAM403 DataProcessed was 351 bytes per request, but its derivation remains unresolved: captured client Content-Length was 23, parsed body reserialization 24, header lines 143. Neither these observations nor the reconstructed request establish a justified byte formula.

Both protocols admitted default DetailedMetricsEnabled true with the off route false; detailed off-route datapoints were nevertheless observed. The default-disabled baseline had no detailed route datapoints.

WebSocket counters use Count; IntegrationLatency uses Milliseconds. Error metrics include zero samples. ConnectCount and MessageCount each incremented for the successful connect and the Lambda-returned 403 connect rejection; the rejection incremented ClientError.

WebSocket one-way route total MessageCount was 2 for two sends, while two-way route total was 4 for two sends and two witnessed responses. Successful Management callbacks contributed two messages under Route POST /@connections/{connectionId}, with no IntegrationLatency series.

Two Lambda proxy 503 responses produced ExecutionError Sum 2 and IntegrationError Sum 0 with two samples; both response bodies reached the client. A missing Lambda alias produced ExecutionError Sum 1 and a witnessed Internal server error response.

The final window included off-route two-way traffic, unknown-route Forbidden, and held-close. It had API MessageCount Sum 3 and ClientError Sum 1; discovered $disconnect MessageCount Sum 1 occurred despite no configured disconnect integration.
All raw observations, query inputs, empty datapoint arrays, units and five statistics are retained. Publication observations are bounded measurements, not exact latency or service timing rules.
scope: One owned HTTP API and one WebSocket API sharing a real Lambda, role and function log group; no API Gateway logging/account changes
